prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: first input paint_mask_guide.png. Second input design_reference.png is appearance reference only. Third input icon_x8.png is colour reference only. Follow this brief exactly:
# Igdrasine: paint + material mask view atlas

Scope: image generation only. Write ONLY into `level_generation/props/items_mm9_claude/codex_tex/d10200/`. Do not edit any other file, do not run builds.

Inputs (attached):
- `paint_mask_guide.png`: 1536x2048 transparent sheet, three columns by FOUR rows of 512x512 cells. Rows 1-2 and rows
  3-4 hold the same five grey orthographic renders of the exact 3D model: FRONT, BACK, LEFT / RIGHT, TOP, empty.

Task: use your built-in image generation tool to paint the guide sheet. Output ONE PNG with a transparent background
and a 3:4 canvas (1536x2048 or the tool's nearest 3:4 size), the same layout, each object in exactly the same position,
size and outline as its grey guide. Paint the grey objects only; never redraw, enlarge, move or redesign them.

- Rows 1-2 (PAINT): the unlit base colour of the item on each view: A sleeveless fitted leather jerkin quartered in green and blue (green upper near side and lower far side, blue upper far side and lower near side), a golden tree with spreading leafy branches embossed on the chest, gold studs on the green quarters, and a gold-rimmed neck, armholes and hem..
- Rows 3-4 (MATERIAL MASK): the same five silhouettes filled with FLAT pure colours only, no shading, no texture, no
  outlines, no antialiased colour blends inside:
  - pure red #FF0000: every metal part (steel, iron, chain mail, gold, silver, bronze, copper, brass)
  - pure green #00FF00: every leather part (straps, padding, hide, suede) and fur
  - pure blue #0000FF: every cloth part (tabards, quilting, linings, cords, ribbons) and hair
  - pure black #000000: every gemstone, crystal, glass, pearl, enamel or liquid seen through glass
  Every pixel of each silhouette gets exactly one of these colours; nothing outside the silhouettes.
- `design_reference.png`: the approved HD painting or master of the item, the material and detail reference.
- `icon_x8.png`: the original game icon (magenta is background), the colour reference.

Object: A sleeveless fitted leather jerkin quartered in green and blue (green upper near side and lower far side, blue upper far side and lower near side), a golden tree with spreading leafy branches embossed on the chest, gold studs on the green quarters, and a gold-rimmed neck, armholes and hem.

- Facets, engravings, scrollwork and inner swirls follow the design reference, scaled to each view.
- Keep every gap and opening exactly as in the guide and fully transparent.
- Unlit base colour only: no lighting, no cast shadows, no ambient occlusion, no hot highlights or reflections, no
  glow halo, sparkles or aura outside the silhouette, no ground, no outlines, no text.
- The empty cells (column 3 of row 2 and row 4) stay empty and transparent.

Save the generated image (copy the file the tool produced) to `level_generation/props/items_mm9_claude/codex_tex/d10200/paint_mask_raw_v1.png` and write
`generation_paint.json` (prompt, inputs with sha256, original output path, output, size). At most one corrective
regeneration, only if the silhouettes or layout are clearly wrong.

CORRECTION: Match the guide silhouettes and all visible interior surfaces EXACTLY. No stray speckles or pixels outside silhouette. Interior leather surfaces shown grey in the guide must remain solid filled surfaces, not be cut out as holes. Only actual transparent holes in guide stay transparent. Material classification is NOT paint colour: ALL leather, including BOTH the blue-painted and green-painted quarters and inner surfaces, is pure GREEN #00FF00 in bottom two rows. Only gold tree, studs and rims are pure RED #FF0000. This item has no cloth: no blue in material masks. Preserve all ten guide shapes at exact positions and scales. Flat unlit paint in upper half, exact flat binary red/green material regions in lower half.
limitations: Residual edge speckles and silhouette/opening deviations remain in raw generated output; no postprocessing applied.
